Belgrave went to Leicester for their annual Midland pot-hunt with the usual strong team, although two weak links were the absence of Allan Callow (racing in the Isle of Man over 20 miles) and the uncertainty of Carl Lawton being able to last the distance.

Following Carl home after a six second interval was Len Duquemin and then Allan Callow to give us an easy team victory. Belgrave 'B' team was prominent but due to some of our leading men resting they could not get into the prizes.

Our first grievous loss was that of Allan Callow, who after leading our team for some time, found the conditions too much, and dropped out. This eliminated us from the"Nijmegan Shield" for the Club with the first complete team, which until recent memory, was a trophy held by us for many years.
In the 5km Ken Carter of Southend won easily despite a late rally by Allan Callow and Peter Selby. Len Duquemin walked steadily home for 4th.
In the Senior race some fast times were produced with the first six under 92 minutes. Allan Callow was first Belgravian home and John Hall, in 23rd position, produced a personal best.

In the 20 miles Walk Belgrave will have the terrific line-up of Carl Lawton representing England (and whose wife Barbara has been selected for the High Jump), John Moullin and Len Duquemin representing Guernsey and Allan Callow for the Isle of Man.

We bounced back two weeks later to win the Southern Area Track League which showed our strength with the absence of Allan Callow and Len Duquemin but within another two weeks we crashed out of the 'Brighton' with only four starters including Eric Stroud, who in his first attempt had to give in at Crawley.

The 20 miles Walk was held over an out-and-back course with a 5 p.m. start to avoid the worst of the sun, and of the fifteen starters four were Belgravians, with Len Duquemin and John Moullin for Guernsey, Carl Lawton for England and Allan Callow representing the Isle of Man.
This issue of the "Belgravian" coincides with the departure of Allan Callow for New Zealand, to the land that attracted him a few months ago.

Reviewing the result sheet shows "superb packing again bore its fruit" Too much praise cannot be given to Allan Callow for leading our team to victory, ably supported by his team mates John Moullin, Ray Middleton and Carl Lawton.

Not the strongest field that we would have liked to have turned out, but without Allan Callow we could not expect much. Olly Flynn led from 5k to the finish while further back Carl Lawton was well placed in the first 20.

This again leaves our team depleted, especially following Allan Callow's departure mentioned in the previous issue. News from overseas indicates that Allan has settled in to his new abode and Dave De Bondi is changing status at last.
In his last race before emigrating to New Zealand, Allan Callow finished 2nd in 97:37 to Paul Nihill (Croydon) 90:07 over 20 kilometres.

Nevertheless there was a notable turn-out at last January's Commonwealth Games in New Zealand with four representatives, Carl Lawton for England, Len Duquemin and John Moullin for Guernsey and Allan Callow for the Isle of Man.

On January 25th Allan Callow competed in a 5,000m track walk during the New Zealand Games. He took the lead after 1 km but lost a shoe in the tightly packed bunch and after taking time out to replace it, clocked 24:09.2 for 5th.
Allan Callow is probably returning to these shores from New Zealand later this year and will be preceded by Graham Seatter, a leading New Zealand walker.
Our Christchurch based talent scout Allan Callow was responsible for this Kiwi influx when he influenced fellow walker Graham Seatter into joining Belgrave when he came over to the U.K.
However, another Belgravian is planning to return to the UK this summer - Allan Callow. Allan, a past committee member of our club has enjoyed a deal of success while in New Zealand.
In the 30 kilometre walk, held in blistering conditions, Graham Seatter placed 7th for New Zealand while Allan Callow, representing the Isle of Man, was numbered among those who failed to finish.
The sun scorched the sixteen starters unmercifully and it is not surprising that four men failed to finish including our own Allan Callow representing the Isle of Man.
It was good to see the cheery figure of Allan Callow on arrival at the Crystal Palace for this years R.W.A.

Congratulations on some great walking Graham, its good to see you back in such great form - a great day. Allan Callow and Derek Howie (who had competed in the longer race the previous day) were our other representatives.
